record.paper_title: XXX Spin Chain: from Bethe Solution to Open Problems
record.original_question: For the XXZ spin chain in the critical regime -1 ≤ Δ < 1, obtain an explicit analytic asymptotic formula for the time- and temperature-dependent correlation functions, such as g(n,t), in the limit of large spatial separation and large time separation. In particular, derive the formula describing their expected exponential decay in this critical region.

evidence.quote: Despite these considerable efforts the asymptotics of time and temperature dependent correlation functions, such as g(n, t) (see 13) for the XXZ spin chain, are still out of our reach. We expect that they will decay exponentially like in the previous examples of the isotropic XY spin chain or the δ-function Bose gas but at this moment we do not have such a result.
Open problem: Derive an explicit analytic formula describing the asymptotic exponential decay of time and temperature correlation functions in the critical region (−1 ≤ ∆ < 1) of the XXZ spin chain.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the spin-1/2 XXZ Heisenberg chain on the infinite lattice with Hamiltonian
H = J ∑_{n∈ℤ} ( S^x_n S^x_{n+1} + S^y_n S^y_{n+1} + Δ S^z_n S^z_{n+1} ),
where S^α_n = ½ σ^α_n are the spin-1/2 operators acting on site n, J>0, and the anisotropy parameter Δ lies in the critical (massless) regime −1 ≤ Δ < 1. For inverse temperature β>0, define the dynamical two-point correlation function
 g(n,t) = ⟨ S^z_0(0) S^z_n(t) ⟩_β = Tr( e^{−βH} e^{iHt} S^z_n e^{−iHt} S^z_0 ) / Tr( e^{−βH} ),
and analogous transverse correlators ⟨S^+_0(0) S^−_n(t)⟩_β. In the joint regime |n| → ∞ and |t| → ∞ (with any prescribed ratio), derive an explicit closed-form analytic expression for the leading asymptotic behaviour of g(n,t), expected to exhibit exponential decay in both n and t, including the exact decay rates (correlation length and inverse relaxation time) and the prefactors/amplitudes as functions of β and Δ.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made since the problem was posed. Kozlowski (J. Math. Phys. 2019) derived the long-distance and large-time asymptotics of dynamic correlation functions in the massless (critical) regime of the XXZ chain at zero temperature using a thermal/form-factor approach. Dugave–Göhmann–Kozlowski and collaborators developed thermal form-factor expansions yielding large-distance asymptotics of finite-temperature static correlators and partial results on dynamical ones. A fully explicit, rigorous closed-form asymptotic formula for the combined large-n, large-t, finite-T regime −1 ≤ Δ < 1 does not yet appear to be established in complete generality, so the problem is best classified as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Long-distance and large-time asymptotic behaviour of dynamic correlation functions in the massless regime of the XXZ spin-1/2 chain
status_evidence.snippet: Extracts the long-distance and large-time asymptotics of two-point dynamical correlation functions, yielding critical exponents and amplitudes in the massless regime.
status_evidence.claim: Zero-temperature dynamical asymptotics in the massless regime have been derived.

status_evidence.title: Thermal form factors of the XXZ chain and the large-distance asymptotics of its temperature dependent correlation functions
status_evidence.snippet: Form factors of the quantum transfer matrix determine the leading asymptotics of finite-temperature correlation functions of the XXZ chain.
status_evidence.claim: Thermal form factor expansions give large-distance asymptotics of finite-temperature correlators.

status_evidence.title: Multi-point Correlation Functions in the Boundary XXZ Chain at Finite Temperature
status_evidence.snippet: Finite-temperature correlation functions are expressed as sums over thermal form factors in the quantum transfer matrix framework.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent progress on the finite-temperature framework, but full explicit dynamical asymptotics not completed.
